title: The Morning Digest: November 1, 2026
dek: OPEC+ agreed in principle to keep December production targets unchanged (Reuters, Nov 1), the expected outcome, with about 2 million barrels a day of further cuts in place through the end of 2026 and the group's work turning to 2027 baselines. Nakilat confirmed on Nov 1 that its LNG carrier Al Mayeda was hit by unidentified objects in the Arabian Gulf on Friday evening and remained operational, with no crew injured and no environmental impact. Iran's foreign minister said a plan worked out with Qatari mediators could reopen the strait within two days on conditions including sanctions relief, a force pullback and the release of frozen funds, with no public acceptance reported (Al Jazeera, Oct 31). December WCS is -$29.75 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 30) on 990 lots, November Mainline apportionment of Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert is in effect, and the validated diesel crack is $92.28.

sources.vintage: Nov 1, 2026 (OPEC+ agreed in principle to keep December production targets unchanged, per three people familiar with the matter, ahead of a Sunday online meeting of seven core members: Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman; the group completed the rollback of a 1.65 million barrel a day cut in September; a further layer of about 2 million barrels a day of cuts runs through the end of 2026; most Gulf members are pumping below their targets; a fourth quarter capacity review will set the baselines for 2027 quotas)

Nov 1, 2026 (Qatar Gas Transport Company Nakilat confirmed its LNG carrier Al Mayeda was hit by unidentified objects while transiting the Arabian Gulf on Friday evening Oct 30; no crew injured, no impact on the environment, the vessel in a safe condition and operational, the impact being assessed; secondary reporting places the vessel about 40 nautical miles off Iran's Lavan Island, via UKMTO reporting)

Oct 31, 2026 (Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said talks with Qatari mediators produced a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days, conditional on the United States lifting sanctions, pulling back forces and releasing Iran's frozen money; no public White House response or Qatari acceptance reported as of Nov 1)
